d409a070b22b.exp: Without equipment to macerate and disinfect sewage, discharge is only allowed more than 12 miles from the coast. With the right equipment, it is allowed from 3 miles. 4 miles and 4 knots are not sufficient criteria on their own.

bf4186c1cead.exp: Posidonia oceanica is a marine plant that forms meadows of great ecological value. When anchoring, the anchor and chain tear up or damage the plants and destroy the meadow, which grows very slowly. Sailing or trawling in them is not prohibited in itself.

112ec0787c6c.exp: On buoyed-off beaches, the bathing area is for swimmers only: entry and anchoring of any vessel or floating craft, personal watercraft included, is prohibited. There is no 3-knot speed exception for them. Sailing at 3 knots applies to other cases, such as cliffs or access channels.

a9e4f230831b.exp: The minimum safety distance from a diving area, marked with the Alpha or modified Bravo flag, is 50 metres, and only the support vessel may be closer. Do not confuse it with other distances such as 25, 75 or 100 metres.

53dc05e73b26.exp: Dumping plastics into the sea is totally prohibited anywhere, including the Mediterranean, under MARPOL Annex V. Food waste and sewage may be discharged under certain distance and treatment conditions, but plastics may not.

06fbc101749d.exp: Under Royal Decree 1727/2007, when near a group of cetaceans you must reduce speed, not come closer than 60 metres, make no noise and not chase them, nor accelerate or change course abruptly. Within 500 metres speed is limited to 4 knots. Getting as close as possible or scaring them is prohibited.

0d7532e49b9e.exp: At the harbour entrance, vessels leaving have priority over those entering, because they have less visibility and less manoeuvrability, and the vessel entering can easily wait. It does not depend on sound or light signals, nor is it a matter of indifference.

6eb6725022d1.exp: Outside special areas, unground food waste may be thrown overboard from 12 miles off the coast. If ground up, 3 miles would be enough. Here the correct option is 12 miles, which does not require grinding. 4 miles is not a MARPOL limit.

29bb68f3e3aa.exp: When sailing less than 50 metres from cliffs, the maximum speed is 3 knots for safety: there may be swimmers, divers or falling rocks. The generic safe speed does not apply. 3 knots is about 5.5 km/h.

8402d68d49c8.exp: The modified Bravo flag is red with a white diagonal stripe, and indicates the presence of submerged divers. It differs from the International Code Bravo (red with a swallowtail cut), which indicates dangerous goods. Remember red and white, as on diving buoys.

c081b1892868.exp: All vessels, except the divers' support vessel, must keep a minimum radius of 50 metres from the buoy with the Alpha or modified Bravo flag, to avoid injuring divers with propellers. 5, 25 or 75 metres are not valid distances.

3a50c1fb8dee.exp: Sewage may only be discharged 3 miles or more from the coast, and only with macerating and disinfecting equipment. At 2 miles, therefore, it cannot be discharged at any speed: speed is only an additional requirement and does not replace distance.

4ba8b5bc0627.exp: When entering or leaving port, the vessel leaving has priority over the one entering, since it has less visibility and manoeuvrability at the harbour entrance. Priority does not depend on the size of the boat or on whether it is a fishing vessel or a merchant ship.

87a996c37e13.exp: Throwing plastics into the sea from any ship is totally prohibited under MARPOL Annex V, whatever the distance or treatment. By contrast, food waste and sewage may be discharged under certain conditions. It is not true that nothing can be thrown overboard: some waste is permitted under conditions.

cc86e967acfe.exp: The SPAMIs (Specially Protected Areas of Mediterranean Importance; ZEPIM) in Catalonia are the Medes Islands and Cap de Creus. The other options mix places that are not Catalan SPAMIs or are outside Catalonia, such as Alborán or Cabo de Gata.

23588a4706e0.exp: Posidonia oceanica is a flowering aquatic plant, not an alga, that forms underwater meadows essential in the Mediterranean. It is a marine plant (a seagrass, or phanerogam), with roots, leaves and flowers, although it is mistaken for an alga. That is why it is protected and you must not anchor on it.

9deb845fac8c.exp: ZEPIM stands for Specially Protected Area of Mediterranean Importance (Zona Especialmente Protegida de Importancia para el Mediterráneo), a protection designation of the Barcelona Convention to conserve the biodiversity and natural heritage of the Mediterranean. It is not a research, fishing or study area. The Catalan ZEPIMs are the Medes and Cap de Creus.

733f57e5c2ed.exp: Outside special areas, food waste may be thrown overboard 3 miles or more from the coast if it is ground up (particles smaller than 25 mm). Unground, you must be 12 miles or more away. There is no 2-mile limit, nor may it be thrown at any distance.

9a340ea9eda5.exp: The modified Bravo flag, which indicates divers in the water, is red with a white diagonal stripe: its colours are white and red. It has no blue or yellow. Do not confuse it with Alpha, which is white and blue.

2a7045604e2a.exp: The International Code of Signals Alpha flag is white and blue, divided vertically with a swallowtail cut on the fly side. It means diver down, keep clear and go slowly. Red and white belong to the modified Bravo.

5b4d67a2d975.exp: The modified Bravo diving flag is red with a white diagonal stripe: the colours are red and white. It has no blue or yellow. Alpha is the white and blue one. Remember that both indicate divers and both require keeping 50 metres clear.

92b22da0771e.exp: Under Royal Decree 2335/1980, the flag of the autonomous community may be flown together with that of Spain on pleasure craft, but its size may not exceed 1/3 of the area of the national flag, which is the main one. It is not mandatory to fly only the Spanish flag, nor may the other equal it.

a5957e7ffb65.exp: With the Alpha or modified Bravo flag, all vessels must keep a minimum distance of 50 metres from the diving area, except the support vessel. 25 and 15 metres are not valid. Remember: 50 metres clearance.

79a83e6aa689.exp: Discharging sewage at any distance is only allowed to protect the safety of the vessel and the people on board, or to save lives at sea. It is the exception provided in MARPOL for emergencies. Speed alone never allows it.

72d19223490e.exp: The SOLAS Convention (Safety of Life at Sea), Regulation 33 of Chapter V, requires the master of any ship in a position to help to proceed at full speed to the scene of the casualty and to inform the people in distress or the search and rescue service. MARPOL deals with pollution and ZEPIM with protected areas.

9b10da2730e9.exp: In port areas all discharge of sewage is prohibited, even if treated, because they are areas with little water renewal and recreational use. The distance and treatment conditions apply only on the open sea. The port's collection facilities must be used.

1bed9ccc80f7.exp: At 4 miles from the coast, sewage may be discharged if there is approved macerating and disinfecting equipment (3 miles or more) and the vessel is sailing at least 4 knots. Beyond 12 miles no equipment is required, but the minimum speed of 4 knots is also required for discharge.

f513aacab113.exp: The ZEPIMs were created to protect a set of Mediterranean coastal and marine areas of ecological and heritage value, in accordance with the Barcelona Convention. They were not created to sink ships or to facilitate diving or nautical activities.

d67157e3f059.exp: Posidonia oceanica is the main source of oxygenation of the Mediterranean, protects the coast from erosion and is a habitat and refuge for many species. The anchor and chain damage it, which is why you must not anchor on it. It is not a bathing zone, a spearfishing zone or a no-sailing area.

528928405bc7.exp: Anchoring on Posidonia oceanica damages the plants and destroys the meadow, which regenerates very slowly and is key to the ecosystem. MARPOL does not prohibit it, nor are these areas reserved for swimmers or personal watercraft. Look for sandy bottoms to anchor.

87c700b06f85.exp: The SOLAS Convention, Chapter V, Regulation 33, regulates the obligation to assist persons in distress at sea. ZEPIM is an environmental protection designation, and IMO is the international organisation that adopts conventions, not a convention itself.

313cad5d0910.exp: Under Royal Decree 550/2020, art. 14, vessels, except the support vessel, must keep a minimum distance of 50 metres from the diving area, not 25. The option marked (25 metres) contradicts the text of the very statement cited, which speaks of 50 metres.
313cad5d0910.duda: The regulation cited in the options themselves (RD 550/2020, art. 14) sets a safety distance of 50 metres; key d (25 metres) appears to be wrong, and the question is already flagged as open to challenge.

e92094a4201a.exp: On buoyed-off beaches reserved for swimmers, entry and anchoring of any type of vessel is prohibited, with no exceptions for length or type (personal watercraft included). The bathing zone is exclusively for swimmers, and buoyed channels are the access lanes.

156387386539.exp: The current ZEPIM areas in Catalonia are the Medes Islands and Cap de Creus, two protected marine areas of the Catalan coast. The other options include places that are not Catalan ZEPIMs, such as the Llobregat or Foix areas, or the Ebro Delta and Els Alfacs.

9181afdece9d.exp: The current ZEPIM areas in Catalonia are the Medes Islands and Cap de Creus, and option b, although truncated, is the one that mentions Cap de Creus. The other options cite places that are not ZEPIMs, such as the Llobregat, the Foix, Cap de Salou or Els Alfacs.

7e83ac22ea6d.exp: Plastics are always prohibited everywhere under MARPOL Annex V. Food waste and sewage may be discharged if distance and treatment conditions are met. Plastics are kept on board and handed in at port.

af05ab3050d0.exp: Dumping plastics into the Mediterranean is totally prohibited in all circumstances (MARPOL Annex V). Food waste and sewage allow certain distance and treatment conditions. They are kept on board and handed in at port.

02ad957f4d9d.exp: Plastics are the only thing that is always prohibited to throw into the sea, anywhere and under any condition, under MARPOL Annex V. Food waste and sewage may be discharged with distance and prior treatment. Saying that everything is always prohibited would be incorrect.

8588f337622b.exp: The two flags in the drawing, Alpha (white and blue) and modified Bravo (red with a white diagonal stripe), indicate the presence of a submerged diver. Both are used to mark diving activity. They do not indicate isolated danger, grounding or a prohibition on dumping waste.

9c93bf4c7e14.exp: On buoyed-off beaches, entry and anchoring of any vessel or floating craft, including personal watercraft, is prohibited. The bathing zone is exclusively for swimmers. The 3-knot speed refers to access channels, not to sailing freely within the buoyed-off area.

8889cb8c9bcb.exp: Regulation 33 of SOLAS Chapter V requires the master who receives a signal from persons in distress to proceed at full speed to their assistance, informing them, if possible, or the search and rescue service. He must not stay away nor merely notify 112 or the club.

b79fa565c8c0.exp: A buoy with a red flag with a white diagonal stripe is the modified Bravo, which indicates a submerged diver. It is easily confused with the International Code Bravo (red with a swallowtail cut), which indicates dangerous goods.

114c2b4dfaa2.exp: The isolated danger mark is black with horizontal red bands, with two black spheres as topmark, and its light is white, with groups of 2 flashes (Fl(2)). The two flashes recall the two spheres. Red is not used in its light.

932fdf1d2543.exp: In Region A, when entering port, red beacons are left to port. If we see a red beacon ahead, with a cylindrical topmark, we must leave it to port, and therefore we bear away to starboard. It is remembered as 'red to port when entering'. We would leave it to starboard only if it were green.

f5066681220f.exp: The North cardinal mark indicates that the navigable water is to the north of it, so the danger lies to the south of the mark. A cardinal mark indicates the side on which to pass: the N is passed to the north. The danger is in the opposite quadrant.

d40188a9dd56.exp: The green beacon with a central red band and a green cone is a modified Region A lateral mark that indicates the preferred channel to port. The predominant colour is green (left to starboard when entering) and the red band indicates that the preferred channel lies to port of the beacon, and the green cone confirms it.

9a393d09b9dd.exp: In Region A, a green beacon with a central red band and a green cone as topmark indicates the preferred channel to port. It is a modified lateral mark: it is left to starboard when entering, and the preferred channel lies to its port. The light has the rhythm 2+1 green flashes.

ca29e6e9ffe8.exp: In Region A, when entering port, red beacons are left to port and therefore must be on our port side, which is the one we already have. It is enough to continue on course without bearing away to either side. Remember: when entering, red to port and green to starboard.

423badd03367.exp: In Region A, when entering port, red beacons must be left to port. If we see it on the starboard side, we are on the wrong side and must bear away to starboard to cross and leave it to port. Red to port when entering; we would leave it to starboard only if it were green.

5418a883d46f.exp: The safe water mark (navigable water) is red and white with vertical stripes and has a red sphere as topmark. The two black spheres belong to the isolated danger mark, the two black cones to the cardinal marks and the yellow X to the special marks.

2c2f862ad629.exp: The lateral mark for the preferred channel to port shows a green light with composite groups of 2+1 flashes (Fl(2+1) G). The preferred channel to starboard shows 2+1 red. Groups of 2 belong to the isolated danger and groups of 3 to the East cardinal.

f039d29e626d.exp: Special marks (for exercise areas, cables, anchorages, etc.) carry a yellow X as topmark and their light is yellow, like the mark itself. They are not lateral beacons, so they do not use red or green lights.

8138394072fe.exp: A cardinal that gives three flashes every five seconds is the East one (VQ(3) 5s), whose topmark is two black cones one above the other, base to base (diamond shape). Remember: East has 3 flashes, like 3 o'clock on the clock face.

af491a522028.exp: The isolated danger mark is black with one or more horizontal red bands, and is placed over a small danger surrounded by navigable water. Its topmark is two black spheres and its light is white with 2 flashes.

7335d7d361d4.exp: When leaving through the harbour entrance in Region A, red beacons are left to starboard and green ones to port. With a red light ahead we must bear away to port to leave it to starboard. Remember: when leaving, red to starboard, the opposite of when entering.

d5e9dc041dc0.exp: The safe water mark (navigable water), with vertical red and white stripes, has a white light (isophase, occulting, long flash every 10 s or Morse letter A). It does not show a red light even though its body is partly red.

686b00a9a1e0.exp: Cardinal marks always have a white light. What distinguishes the quadrant is the rhythm: north, continuous flashes; east, 3 flashes; south, 6 plus one long; west, 9 flashes. The west quadrant has a white light with 9 flashes.

50dc171fd5f1.exp: A cardinal mark indicates in which quadrant there is safe water: the E cardinal indicates that the navigable water is to the east of the mark, so the danger lies to the west. You pass to the east, leaving the mark to the west. Mnemonic: the name of the mark is the side on which to pass, not where the danger is.

fefcc5f98172.exp: The isolated danger light is white and shows groups of 2 flashes (Fl(2)), like its two topmark spheres. Mnemonic: two spheres, two flashes. The 2+1 rhythm belongs to the lateral marks for the preferred channel, and groups of 3, 6 or 9 to the cardinal marks.

2236ecd8743e.exp: The isolated danger buoy (horizontal black and red bands) has two black spheres one above the other as topmark. Mnemonic: two spheres = isolated danger, a single point with danger around it and navigable water all around. The single red sphere indicates safe water and the yellow cylinder is not an IALA topmark.

ec2899478718.exp: Horizontal black and red bands with two black spheres as topmark identify an isolated danger, a small obstacle with navigable water around it. It can be passed on any side keeping a safe distance. Do not confuse with the cardinal marks, which are black and yellow and carry cones.

8620cbb6c941.exp: Six quick flashes followed by one long flash correspond to the South cardinal mark (the long flash is added so as not to confuse it with the 9 quick flashes of the west). The South mark indicates that the navigable water is in its south quadrant. Clock-face mnemonic: 3 = east, 6 = south, 9 = west, continuous = north.

5230f127e0fe.exp: Special marks are yellow, and their light, when they have one, is also yellow. They mark specific areas or installations (aquaculture, military exercises, outfalls, regattas) and are not aids to navigation. Their topmark is a yellow X.

c864bdcfd058.exp: The red sphere topmark corresponds to the safe water mark (vertical red and white stripes), whose light is white. Red and green lights belong to lateral marks and yellow to special marks.

009f1489b8ad.exp: In Region A, when entering, green marks are starboard marks and must be on our starboard side. If we see it to port, we must bear away to port to go round it and leave it to starboard. Mnemonic when entering: green to the right, red to the left; as the green one is to port, we move towards it.

394f9e1b4936.exp: Sailing east we are already in the west quadrant of the mark, which is the navigable quadrant. We can go round it to the north or south without a problem, always without passing on the east side, where the danger is. So it makes no difference whether we bear away to port or starboard.

50b39e0ba268.exp: Two cones one above the other with the points downward form the South cardinal mark (yellow below, black above). The navigable water is in the south quadrant of the buoy and the danger to the north. Mnemonic: points downward = south, as if pointing at the ground; upward = north.

b6dc292b2627.exp: In Region A, when entering port, port marks are red with a red cylindrical topmark and starboard marks are green with a green cone. Mnemonic: red-cylinder-port, green-cone-starboard. The red ones are left to port.

9663a00346de.exp: Two black spheres one above the other are the topmark of the isolated danger. Cardinals carry black cones, laterals a red or green cylinder or cone, and safe water marks a red sphere.

5e2a0bbcf7e5.exp: Two cones with the points upward are the North cardinal mark: the navigable water is to the north and the danger to the south. You must pass to the north of the buoy, so we leave it to the south of us. Mnemonic: cones upward, towards the north of the map.

266c4ae844e1.exp: Three flashes every five seconds are the light of the East cardinal (clock: 3 o'clock). The navigable water is to the east of the mark, so we pass to the east and leave it to our west, just as the question asks.

bce24c5efedd.exp: The South cardinal indicates navigable water to the south of the mark. Therefore the danger lies to the north. You pass to the south of the mark, always keeping away from the north side.

1d41c02ed981.exp: The South mark carries two black cones one above the other with the points downward. Mnemonic: points downward = south, upward = north; east = bases facing each other, west = points facing each other (wine-glass shape, W).

c925777fd75c.exp: Preferred channel to port: it is a modified starboard mark, green with a horizontal red band and a green cone topmark with the point upward. When entering we leave it to starboard, but the preferred channel runs on its port side. The red cylinder is used for the preferred channel to starboard.

15e915d40060.exp: Black and yellow bands belong to the cardinal system. They mark a danger and the quadrant in which one can navigate, according to their topmark and light. They do not indicate a channel or direction of traffic.

5301cf061af4.exp: Two cones one above the other with the points upward are the North cardinal: the navigable quadrant is the north. Sailing west, the buoy is ahead and you must pass to its north, bearing away to starboard.

5950ca4ec4e3.exp: Nine flashes every fifteen seconds are the West cardinal (9 o'clock on the clock face). The navigable water is to the west, so we must pass to the west of the mark. Sailing south, west is to starboard: we bear away to starboard.

8a5336736cc1.exp: When leaving port the direction is reversed: red marks, which are to port on entering, must now be left to starboard. Rule of the conventional direction of buoyage: red marks are left to port when entering and to starboard when leaving, for any type of vessel.

d775357342ce.exp: The cardinal quadrants are bounded by the intercardinal bearings from the mark: the South quadrant runs from SE (135) to SW (225), the North from NW to NE, the East from NE to SE and the West from SW to NW. The four quadrants divide the 360 into 90 sectors centred on each cardinal point.

ccd49b7aa6ba.exp: The East cardinal carries two black cones base to base (egg or diamond shape). Mnemonic: East = bases together (diamond shape), West = points together (wine glass with a W), North = both up, South = both down.

ab53c29cc59c.exp: The preferred channel to port is marked with a modified starboard mark: green with a red band and a green cone topmark with the point upward. The green cylinder does not exist in Region A and the red cone is not used that way.

a116ed8e264d.exp: The white light that shows the letter A in Morse (dot dash) is that of the safe water mark, which has an isophase, long-occulting or Morse A light. Mnemonic: A for Aguas (waters). It is not a lateral nor an isolated danger, whose rhythm is groups of 2 flashes.

d74611a84f0b.exp: Nine flashes are the West cardinal. The navigable water is to the west of the mark, so you pass to the west and we leave it to the east of us; hence the answer is East.

3dd2221b4af4.exp: Special marks are yellow, with a yellow X topmark. They do not indicate dangers or channels, but special areas (aquaculture, military exercises, etc.). Red, green, white or black belong to other systems.

5a60b1b2519f.exp: Safe water marks (vertical red and white stripes, red sphere topmark) have a white light, with isophase, occulting, long flash every 10 s or Morse A rhythm. Red and green belong to lateral marks, and yellow to special marks.

1158c76e0d02.exp: In Region A, when entering port, the green mark is a starboard mark and must be left to starboard. If it is already on our starboard side, we are well placed and it is enough to continue on course. Mnemonic: when entering, green to the right.

633cecf503d0.exp: A green light with groups of 2+1 flashes indicates the preferred channel to port: modified starboard mark, green with a red band and a green cone topmark with the point upward. The 2+1 rhythms in red correspond to the preferred channel to starboard, with a red cylinder.

37c13ded6a72.exp: Two black cones with the points upward are the North cardinal. You must pass to the north of the buoy. Sailing west, north is to starboard, so we bear away to starboard. Careful: it is not an isolated danger, which would carry two black spheres.

30c69a4344ac.exp: Two triangles with the points downward are the two cones of the South mark. The navigable water is to the south and the danger to the north of the mark. Mnemonic: points downward, south.

35ed39beea8c.exp: Lateral marks (red and green) indicate the port and starboard sides at port entrances, channels and rivers, in the conventional direction of buoyage, that is, coming from the open sea. Cardinal marks indicate dangers with respect to quadrants.

cb42d678af7a.exp: In Region A, when entering port, the starboard mark is green with a green conical topmark. Mnemonic: green-cone-starboard, red-cylinder-port; the cone points to starboard (right) when entering.

9851d0764c67.exp: Yellow and black bands with cone topmarks are a cardinal mark: it marks a danger and the quadrant in which one can navigate, determined by the shape of the cones. It is not an isolated danger, which is black and red with spheres.

c5479861e78f.exp: Black and yellow bands are a cardinal mark: they indicate the quadrant with navigable water, the danger being on the opposite side. They do not mark ports or traffic.

cae54a1f1c3e.exp: Cardinal marks (black and yellow with cone topmarks) mark a danger and the quadrant of safe water. The isolated danger is a different type of mark: black and red with two spheres.

4f6243732aae.exp: All cardinal marks show a white light. What distinguishes the quadrant is the rhythm: North continuous, East 3 flashes, South 6 and one long, West 9 (clocks: 12, 3, 6, 9).

2f15378ac34f.exp: In Region A, starboard marks are green, with a green conical topmark (point upward). Port marks are red with a cylinder. Mnemonic: green-cone, red-cylinder; Region B reverses the colours.

50cddb5c0e33.exp: Safe water marks have vertical red and white stripes, with a red sphere topmark. They indicate that there is navigable water all around, as in the middle of a channel or on the approach to a port.

28813ce9f5e4.exp: When leaving port, the mark we leave to starboard is the red one (on entering it is the port one): its light is red. In Region A, red marks are port marks when entering and starboard marks when leaving; the light follows the colour of the mark, not the direction of navigation.

ad93683c8bb8.exp: Green beacon with a red band and a green cone: preferred channel to port. The preferred channel lies to port of the mark, so we bear away to port and leave it to starboard. If we continued on course we would be going along the secondary channel.

cf0fdacc36e3.exp: Red beacon with a green band and a red cylinder: preferred channel to starboard. The preferred channel lies to starboard of the mark, so we bear away to starboard, leaving the mark to our port, like an ordinary port mark.

ddbd4c39108a.exp: Two cones one above the other, base to base, are the East cardinal: navigable water to the east, danger to the west. Sailing south we pass to the east of the mark and leave it to the west. Mnemonic: bases together = East.

e97b02362991.exp: The topmark of a special buoy is a yellow X (saltire). Special marks are not aids to navigation, but mark special areas, such as aquaculture or military zones.

b42fa852fa86.exp: Vertical red and white stripes with a red sphere topmark are the safe water mark: there is safe water all around and it can be passed on either side. An isolated danger would be black and red, with two black spheres.

783438d858be.exp: Red stripes with a green one in the centre and a red cylinder: it is a modified port mark that indicates the preferred channel to starboard. The preferred channel runs on the starboard side of the mark. The green cone with a red band would indicate the preferred channel to port.

8cddeedbc2ad.exp: Nine quick flashes every fifteen seconds correspond to the West cardinal mark (nine = 9 o'clock on the clock face). It indicates that the west quadrant of the danger is the navigable one. Do not confuse it with the South, which adds a long flash to its six quick flashes.

38071c6ed9de.exp: All cardinal marks show a white light. What distinguishes one from another is the number of flashes (N continuous, E 3, S 6 + long, W 9).

b86521497f87.exp: In Region A the starboard lateral mark is green and shows a green light. Region B has the colours reversed. Mnemonic: when entering, starboard-green.

01bb30edbfef.exp: The starboard lateral mark, both in Region A and in those for the preferred channel to port, carries a green light. Mnemonic: green to starboard (right), red to port (left) when entering port.

ecb4840d005b.exp: In Region A, the port lateral mark is red, with a red cylindrical topmark. Mnemonic: red-cylinder-port; the starboard one is green-cone.

244238841d89.exp: The starboard lateral mark shows a green light in Region A. Only lateral marks use red and green lights: cardinal and safe water marks, white; special marks, yellow.

06c8df61f949.exp: The preferred channel to port is a modified starboard mark (green with a red band), so its light is green, with a 2+1 flash rhythm. The red light corresponds to the preferred channel to starboard.

3422c275a3e1.exp: The preferred channel to starboard is a modified port mark (red with a green band), so its light is red, with a 2+1 flash rhythm. The green light corresponds to the preferred channel to port.

976cd4783b40.exp: South cardinal mark: the navigable water is to the south and we must pass to its south. Sailing east, south is to starboard, so we bear away to starboard. Leaving it to starboard would mean passing to the north, where the danger is.

20e472746e21.exp: A continuous quick-flashing white light is the North cardinal, with the navigable water to the north. We pass to the north and the mark is left to our south, so the answer is South. Mnemonic: North = continuous light, no groups.

c852633c90e5.exp: The mark in the figure has two cones with their points facing each other (hourglass shape), which is the West cardinal: navigable water to the west, danger to the east. Mnemonic: points together, like a W.

11a819ab0c4a.exp: The figure shows two cones with the points upward: North cardinal, with navigable water to the north and danger to the south.

069d53ac0c16.exp: The West cardinal indicates navigable water to the west of the mark, so the danger lies to the east. You pass to the west, keeping away from the danger.

b27bd0d7df4b.exp: In Region A, the cylinder is the topmark of port marks (red). When entering port they are left to port. Mnemonic: red cylinder, port; green cone, starboard.

ac5402815d9b.exp: Nine very quick flashes and a pause are the West cardinal: the navigable quadrant is the west of the danger. For the South it would be six quick flashes plus one long flash.

28d319460cf9.exp: The mark in the figure carries a yellow X, characteristic of special marks (yellow). They do not indicate dangers or channels, but special areas or installations.

af91902b2a46.exp: Two black balls one above the other are the topmark of the isolated danger, on a buoy with black and red bands. Cardinals carry cones and special marks a yellow X.

d05ee6764a5b.exp: Preferred channel to port is a modified starboard mark: green light with groups of 2+1 flashes. Red with 2+1 would be the preferred channel to starboard.

710059f0ac61.exp: The West cardinal carries two black cones with their points facing each other (opposed by their points), like a goblet or a W. Mnemonic: West = points together; East = bases together.

c33758cc864c.exp: The South cardinal carries two black cones with the points downward. Mnemonic: cones downward = south, upward = north.

291db1b9eb15.exp: Preferred channel to starboard is a modified port mark: red with a green band and a red cylinder topmark. The green cone with the point upward corresponds to the preferred channel to port.

929e5a13c061.exp: Aquaculture is marked with yellow special buoys, whose topmark is a yellow X (yellow saltire). The black spheres belong to the isolated danger and the two black cones to the cardinal marks.

6a53faef74c4.exp: The beacon with black and red bands, with two black spheres as topmark, is an isolated danger: a small obstacle with navigable water around it.

0ce58a8bd28f.exp: Vertical red and white stripes with a red sphere topmark are a safe water mark: there is safe water all around and it can be passed on any side. It is not a mooring beacon.

5d96b35f1a20.exp: A red beacon with a central green band is a modified port mark that indicates the preferred channel to starboard. The preferred channel lies to starboard of the mark.

b09a65106e9a.exp: The red sphere topmark indicates safe water around the beacon (vertical red and white stripes). The isolated danger carries two black spheres and there is no mooring beacon in the IALA system.

73f2a1880d12.exp: Three white flashes every five seconds are the East cardinal: the navigable quadrant is the east of the danger. Mnemonic: clock face, 3 = east.

2eacaeb0abcc.exp: When leaving port, red marks must be left to starboard (the direction is reversed compared with entering). If it is on our port side, we must pass on its port side to leave it to starboard.

209991ccbc0d.exp: The cylinder is the topmark of red marks (port when entering). On leaving it is left to starboard, so if it is ahead we must pass on its port side, bearing away to port.

0ff3e07b35e0.exp: Red stripes with a central green stripe indicate the preferred channel to starboard (modified port mark). The other options are either wrong or repeat the port one.

8d5dfc2f0610.exp: When leaving port, red marks are left to starboard and green ones to port, since buoyage is oriented in the conventional direction (entering): red to port and green to starboard. On leaving it is reversed.

60b537ac94a1.exp: Isophase (Iso) means that the periods of light and darkness last the same. It is not a fixed light or a quick flashing light: a fixed light shines continuously, a quick-flashing light gives 50-300 flashes per minute and Morse uses letters.

25dc9ab7b248.exp: All cardinals show a white light. The East gives groups of three quick flashes (3 o'clock on the clock face). Nine quick flashes are the West and continuous quick flashing, the North.

b1bbb9b79b27.exp: The NE-SE quadrant is the East. Cardinals always show a white light. There are no black lights.

6353c645be60.exp: The safe water mark has a white light (isophase, occulting, long flash or Morse A). Red and green are lateral and yellow special.

1b74b61273b9.exp: If it has a light, the safe water mark shows a white light. The red light is reserved for red lateral marks and yellow for special marks.

514625f79448.exp: In Region A the port lateral mark is red and its light is red. In Region B it is green. Mnemonic: when entering, port-red.

9f65a6e37a9d.exp: Two black spheres identify an isolated danger, whose light is white with groups of 2 flashes. Red and green belong to lateral marks and yellow to special marks.

f5526c88c609.exp: The mark we leave to starboard when entering in Region A is the green one, with a green light. Mnemonic: when entering, green to starboard.

dee0b61353e3.exp: In Region A, the port lateral mark is red and shows a red light. Mnemonic: when entering, red to port (left).

6eb9abc5b849.exp: A red light with groups of 2+1 flashes indicates the preferred channel to starboard (modified port mark, red with a green band). The preferred channel runs to starboard of the mark.

1cffc97cd00f.exp: When entering a port in Region A, a red light corresponds to a port mark, which we must leave to port. If it is ahead, we bear away to starboard to pass on its starboard side and leave it to port.

fdbdd6547ef9.exp: A green cone is the topmark of starboard marks in Region A. When entering port they are left to our starboard. Mnemonic: green-cone-starboard.

c915dfe38db6.exp: Nine flashes every fifteen seconds are the West cardinal: you pass to the west of the light, where the navigable water is. Mnemonic: 9 = west, like 9 o'clock on the clock face.

8d31e1482bca.exp: Two triangles with the points upward are the North cardinal mark: navigable water to the north and danger to the south. Mnemonic: points upward, towards the north.

8c4f988fae91.exp: The West quadrant is bounded by the true bearings SW (225) and NW (315). Options c and d express the same thing in a different order, which is why both are accepted.

2b1d16f40bb4.exp: The North quadrant is bounded by the true bearings NW (315) and NE (045), a 90 sector centred on north. SE-SW delimits the South, NE-SE the East and SW-NW the West.

e38b1be5f620.exp: Military exercise areas are marked with special marks: yellow, with a yellow X topmark and a yellow light. They are not a danger to navigation in general but a regulated area.

0126d8e6f9b5.exp: Two black balls as topmark indicate an isolated danger. Special marks carry a yellow X and safe water marks a red sphere.

ec4bfd1a5a52.exp: The preferred channel to starboard is a modified port mark: red light with a rhythm of composite groups of 2+1 flashes. Strictly speaking the rhythm is flashes, not quick flashes (which are very rapid flashes), but option b is the only one with 2+1.

e987d16c4307.exp: In Region A, the preferred channel to starboard is marked with a red beacon with a green band, whose red light shows composite groups of 2+1 flashes. The composite rhythm indicates a channel junction and the colour of the light is that of the beacon: red. That is why b (1+2) and a (2) are not preferred channel and c is green.

9ad402f7bea5.exp: Navigable water in NE-SE means the mark is to the west of the danger, that is, it is the East cardinal mark. Its topmark is two cones base to base (diamond shape) and its colours are black-yellow-black. Mnemonic: the cones point towards the black bands; on the East, the bases join and the diamond recalls an egg (E for East).

007543d750cf.exp: The cardinal mark indicates, according to its quadrant (N, S, E or W), on which side of it there is navigable water and therefore where to pass the danger. The lateral marks the edges of the channel, the isolated danger is passed on any side and the special mark indicates specific areas or installations without indicating a side.

3a7122bf18f9.exp: The safe water mark (navigable water) has a red sphere as topmark and is painted with vertical red and white stripes. It indicates that there is navigable water around it, so it can be passed on any side. Do not confuse with the isolated danger (two black spheres) or with special marks (yellow saltire).

a910978887d0.exp: Special marks are yellow and their topmark is a yellow saltire (X). They are used to delimit anchoring areas, dumping grounds, installations, cables, recreation areas, etc. They do not indicate safety of navigation but a specific area or installation. The black spheres belong to the isolated danger and the red sphere to safe water.

e08a743253e8.exp: A dumping ground is marked with a special mark: a yellow buoy with a yellow saltire in the shape of an X as topmark. Special marks have no channel-buoyage meaning, but inform about a specific area or installation, which is identified on the chart. The two black spheres belong to the isolated danger.

3d587aa08912.exp: Special marks, which are yellow, carry a yellow saltire (X) as topmark. Here 'special danger' refers to an area or installation marked with a special mark (discharge, cables, military exercises). It must not be confused with the isolated danger, which carries two black spheres.

332f45905a48.exp: Three quick flashes followed by darkness is the VQ(3) rhythm of the East cardinal mark, and therefore the navigable waters are to the east of the mark (the danger lies to the west). Clock trick: 3 flashes is the 3 o'clock position on the clock face, the East. South would be 6 flashes plus one long, West 9 and North continuous.

2980852d8ba8.exp: Continuous quick flashes, without groups, correspond to the North cardinal mark: navigable water to the north of the mark. Clock trick: North has no group (12 or continuous), East 3, South 6 plus a long flash, West 9.

4faaa93f8d76.exp: In the IALA Region A system, when entering port red marks are left to port and green ones to starboard. When leaving it is the opposite, so a red light must be left to starboard. Rule: 'red to port when entering'; when leaving, the red mark is to starboard, and this rule holds for any type of vessel.

db44322e3b47.exp: Six quick flashes plus one long flash identify the South cardinal mark, which must be passed on its south side (navigable water to the south). Sailing east, with the beacon ahead and passing on its south, it ends up on our port side (north is to our left). The danger is to the north of the mark.

014a12968b7d.exp: Nine quick flashes correspond to the West cardinal, which is passed on its west side. Sailing north, west is to port, so the beacon ends up on our starboard side when passing to its west. It is not an isolated danger, which shows flashes in groups of 2.

424430012b3c.exp: In Region A, when entering port the red (cylindrical) mark is to port and the green (conical) to starboard. Mnemonic: entering, red to port and green to starboard, just like the vessel's navigation lights (red to port, green to starboard).

1fd6ffc43149.exp: IALA Region A: entering port, red marks to port and green to starboard, because the channel is considered to be followed in the direction of entry. Mnemonic: red-port, green-starboard; 'red light on the left' like the vessel's navigation lights.

b8521084464c.exp: An isophase (Iso) light has equal periods of light and darkness. Continuous light is fixed (F), flashes in Morse code are Mo and rapid flashes between 50 and 300 per minute are quick (Q or VQ). Iso is used e.g. on safe water marks and lateral marks.

60c8e54130b9.exp: In Region A the starboard lateral mark is green with a green cone topmark with the point upward. The port one is red with a red cylinder. Mnemonic: the cone (point, starboard) and the cylinder (flat, port, like 'red cylinder').

9839d6166c72.exp: The North cardinal mark shows a white continuous quick-flashing light (Q or VQ), without groups. The other cardinals carry groups (E 3, S 6 + long flash, W 9), also with a white light. No cardinal uses a yellow light.

0708d532e9d9.exp: The West cardinal shows a white light in groups of nine quick flashes, VQ(9) every 10 s or Q(9) every 15 s. Clock trick: 9 o'clock is the West. All cardinals use a white light.

40abc20ea257.exp: All cardinal marks show a white light; what distinguishes them is the number of quick flashes (East, three). Red or green light is reserved for lateral marks and yellow for special marks.

73e1317bc482.exp: The red beacon with a green band and a red cylinder marks the preferred channel to starboard (junction). Its light is red, like that of the port lateral marks, with a composite rhythm Fl(2+1). The colour of the light matches the predominant colour of the beacon.

1d7225808cbd.exp: The red sphere is the topmark of safe water marks, whose light is white (Iso, Oc, LFl or Morse A). Red or green are lateral marks, yellow special marks.

05c525dc845d.exp: In Region A the starboard lateral mark is green and its light is green. Port laterals have a red light. Mnemonic: the colour of the light matches that of the mark, green to starboard.

9670789f0d2b.exp: The isolated danger (black and red bands, two black spheres) shows a white light in groups of two flashes, Fl(2). The characteristic feature is the white light with 2 flashes, like its two spheres.

9886aeaa6da5.exp: The two triangles with the point upward are the topmark of the North cardinal, with navigable water to the north and danger to the south of the mark. If we sail south and the mark is ahead, the danger lies ahead, so we must deviate to the north, not continue on course.

10286fda9d58.exp: The green light with 2+1 groups is that of the preferred channel to port (green beacon with a red band). When entering, a green mark is normally left to starboard, but the junction mark indicates that the preferred channel is to port of it, that is, that we must pass on its port side, so we bear away to port.

0d53245434a7.exp: The red cylinder is the port mark in Region A. When entering port it is left to port, that is, it must be on our left, so we bear away to starboard to pass on its right. Leaving the mark to port and bearing away to starboard are the same manoeuvre.

cbce35910d74.exp: In Region A the (red) cylinder is a port mark: when entering port it must be on our port side, that is, it passes on the left of our vessel. Rule: 'red to port when entering'.

b8980aa9496d.exp: The green cone is a starboard mark in Region A: when entering port it must be on our starboard side, to the right. Rule: green-starboard when entering. Cone (point) and starboard, cylinder and port.

636e543d4e60.exp: Two black cones with the points downward are the South cardinal mark: the navigable waters are to the south of the mark. Mnemonic: the cones point to the side of the black bands and the danger is opposite the navigable water, in this case to the north. On the chart it is identified in the option in which 'South' appears.
636e543d4e60.duda: The marked option (c) is blank; the correct answer South appears in the text of option b (corrupt text).

52f8f5dfcbe7.exp: Two cones opposed by their points (joined at the tips) form the West cardinal, which is passed on the west of the mark. Therefore the danger lies to the east. Mnemonic: the W shape or hourglass recalls the 'window' of the West.

d0a9c3918ffe.exp: Nine flashes correspond to the West cardinal, which must be passed on its west. Sailing north with the beacon ahead, west is on our left, so we bear away to port to pass to its west and leave it to starboard.

f2a754cb3bfe.exp: Two cones with the points upward are the North cardinal: you pass to the north of the mark. Sailing west, north is to starboard, so we bear away to starboard to pass to the north. The danger is to the south.

6b80474f2c64.exp: Two cones with the tips upward are the North cardinal: navigable water to the north, danger to the south. On a westerly course, north is on our right, so we bear away to starboard to pass to the north of the buoy. It is not an isolated danger, which carries two spheres.

5b9b5d31355e.exp: Cones opposed by their points form the West cardinal: navigable water to the west and danger to the east. Sailing south, west is on our right, so we pass to the west of the buoy and it is left to our port, that is, on our east side. The key refers to that side of the buoy with respect to us.

af19c07bcd62.exp: Cones with the tips upward are the North cardinal: you pass to the north. On a course of 270 (west), north is to starboard, so we bear away to starboard to leave it to our port.

f6ff06a9781f.exp: A red light with a 2+1 group is that of the preferred channel to starboard (red beacon with a green band). The composite rhythm indicates a channel junction, red = modified port mark. It does not indicate a harbour entrance, isolated danger (white, 2 flashes) or grounding danger.

dd4e6573797a.exp: A red light with composite 2+1 rhythm indicates the preferred channel to starboard in Region A: red beacon with a green band. The green one (preferred channel to port) shows a green light. Mnemonic: the colour of the light is the dominant colour of the mark.

ea2bbc7e4b7e.exp: The East cardinal has its safe water to the east, that is, in the NE-SE quadrant, and the danger to the west. Mnemonic: the mark 'warns' us on which side the danger is and you pass on the side of its bases.

12ba6178f1fb.exp: South cardinal: navigable water to the south, between SW and SE; the danger lies to the north. Two cones with the points downward and a light of 6 quick flashes plus one long.

f96bf18d878b.exp: West cardinal: navigable water in the NW-SW quadrant, that is, to the west of the mark; the danger lies to the east. Option d, avoid passing to the west, is exactly the opposite.

2965f51547c7.exp: Two cones joined by their bases (diamond shape) form the topmark of the East cardinal: the navigable water is to the east of the beacon and the danger lies to the west.

c0ffaff61e39.exp: The red cylinder is a port mark in Region A (entering). Leaving port the situation is reversed: the red mark is to starboard. It is independent of the type of vessel.

b9ace850ff75.exp: Six quick flashes plus one long flash is the South cardinal: navigable water to the south of the mark. Clock trick: the long flash is the 'hand' that completes the 6.

cceb9bd9de9e.exp: Two black spheres one above the other are the isolated danger mark, which shows a white light in groups of 2 flashes. It marks a small danger with navigable water around it; it can be passed on any side.

8db0f20854b2.exp: The East cardinal shows a white VQ(3) light every 5 seconds. The faster rhythm (VQ) is combined with the East's 3 flashes. Q(3) every 10 s is the lower-frequency version, but VQ(3) 5 s is the correct one from this table.

e0404d5d1cb9.exp: Special marks (yellow with an X) mark cables, pipelines, recreation areas, dumping grounds and other installations. They have no function of buoying a channel or indicating a quadrant.

2e02a9005ee6.exp: The figure shows two black spheres on a buoy with black and red bands: it is the isolated danger mark. It is placed over a danger of limited extent and can be passed on any side.

7fafc124596c.exp: The figure shows a conical or cylindrical red or green mark, with a topmark: it is a lateral mark, which delimits the channel.

9ff3163e9ed8.exp: Cardinal marks indicate in which quadrant (north, south, east or west) the deepest or safest water lies with respect to them. Lateral marks buoy the channel, isolated danger marks are passed on any side and special marks indicate areas.

cfab75fc8ea0.exp: The drawing shows two black spheres stacked, the topmark of the isolated danger. Special marks carry an X, lateral marks a cone or cylinder and safe water marks a red sphere.

c1a9296098d6.exp: Aquaculture installations are marked with special marks: yellow, with a yellow saltire topmark and a yellow light. They do not indicate a channel or a water hazard.

4d1e8c3179bf.exp: The preferred channel to port, in Region A, is marked with a green light with a composite rhythm of 2+1 flashes. The beacon is green with a red band. Conversely, the preferred channel to starboard is red with a 2+1 rhythm.

ff7cdfc5c34f.exp: The isolated danger shows a white light in groups of 2 flashes, Fl(2). The drawing shows the two black topmark spheres, which recall the 2. Composite groups 2+1 belong to preferred channel marks, in red or green.

410bc78ee30f.exp: The isolated danger shows a white light with groups of 2 flashes, like its two black spheres. The 2+1 rhythms belong to preferred channel marks.

74c850c95e7d.exp: Navigable water in the north quadrant corresponds to the North cardinal, with the two cones with the points upward, and black on top of the buoy. Mnemonic: the points show the north.

8f7d5afca085.exp: The NW-NE quadrant is the north: North cardinal, with two cones with the points upward (pointing north).

48b35f6f91e2.exp: NW-SW is the west: West cardinal mark, with two cones opposed by their points and black-yellow-black bands. Mnemonic: hourglass shape, 'W'.

69c71fdd8f62.exp: Six flashes plus one long is the South cardinal, with the cone points downward. Mnemonic: the cones point to the south.

1159b7097bbe.exp: Nine flashes correspond to the West cardinal, with two cones opposed by their points (tips joined). The West is the only one with the points joined.

c1b4e3eb9302.exp: The preferred channel to starboard is marked by a red beacon with a green band and a red cylinder topmark. It looks like a port one, but the green band indicates that the preferred channel is to starboard.
